title: Working with capability that does not stand still
summary: AI can exceed people on some tasks while failing on others, and those boundaries keep changing. Mollick argues for learning through use, choosing how to collaborate or delegate, and evaluating the results. Completion is only one goal: learning, judgment, voice and relationships can justify a different arrangement. Deep knowledge, breadth, taste and agency help people direct these systems. At work and in society, benefits depend on incentives, institutions and choices about power as much as on better models. The book considers wider opportunities and dangers without claiming certainty about jobs, consciousness or the path to more general intelligence.
